excerpts.author: fvictorio
excerpts.content:
<@!543900561460822016> is there anything decided about the behavior of the `eth_sendTransaction` RPC method? I've thought a bit about this, and the way I'd implement it in Hardhat would be like this:

- If `gasPrice` is combined with `maxFeePerGas` or `maxPriorityFeePerGas` (or both), throw an "invalid input" error.
- If only `gasPrice` is passed, then this is interpreted as `{ maxFeePerGas: gasPrice, maxPriorityFeePerGas: gasPrice }`
- If only one of `maxFeePerGas` and `maxPriorityFeePerGas` is passed, throw an "invalid input" error
- If `maxPriorityFeePerGas` is bigger than `maxFeePerGas`, throw an "invalid arguments" error

excerpts.author: fvictorio
excerpts.content: But we are probably willing to make changes for better compatibility with geth

> If gasPrice is combined with maxFeePerGas or maxPriorityFeePerGas (or both), throw an "invalid input" error.
yes, this should return an error

> If only gasPrice is passed, then this is interpreted as { maxFeePerGas: gasPrice, maxPriorityFeePerGas: gasPrice }
no, if only `gasPrice` is passed then the transaction will be sent with using it (although 1559 will be definition understand it as you've described)

> If only one of maxFeePerGas and maxPriorityFeePerGas is passed, throw an "invalid input" error
i believe yes, it should throw
